recipes.title: Empty and delete a bucket

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Select the bucket {1} in the list.
Press Empty, confirm, and wait until the bucket is empty.
Select the bucket again and press Delete.
Type the bucket name {1} to confirm and press Delete bucket.

recipes.verify: The bucket is no longer in the General purpose buckets list.

recipes.title: Delete a bucket

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Select the bucket {1} in the list.
Press Delete above the table.
Type the bucket name and press Delete bucket. A bucket with objects must be emptied first.

recipes.verify: The bucket disappears, or the dialog says the bucket is not empty.

recipes.title: Create a bucket

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Press Create bucket.
Type the bucket name {1}.
Leave the other settings and press Create bucket at the bottom.

recipes.verify: The new bucket appears in the General purpose buckets list.

recipes.title: Download an object

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Open the folders down to the object {2} and select it.
Press Download. The file lands in your lab workspace.

recipes.verify: A message says the object was downloaded to your lab workspace.

recipes.title: Upload a file to a bucket

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {2}.
Open the folder for the key {3} (use Create folder if it is missing).
Press Upload.
Tick the workspace file {1}.
Press Upload to send it.

recipes.verify: A green banner says the upload succeeded and the object is listed.

recipes.title: See the objects in a bucket

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Read the Objects tab; open a folder to see what is inside it.
Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Read the bucket names in the General purpose buckets table.

recipes.title: Browse a prefix in a bucket

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Open the folders of the prefix {2}; each folder shown is one common prefix.

recipes.title: Turn on bucket versioning

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Open the Properties tab.
In Bucket Versioning press Edit.
Choose Enable ({2}).
Press Save changes.

recipes.verify: Bucket Versioning on the Properties tab shows the new state.

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Open the Properties tab and read Bucket Versioning and Default encryption.
Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Open the Permissions tab and read Block public access (bucket settings).

recipes.title: Create a lifecycle rule

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Open the Management tab.
Press Create lifecycle rule.
Type the rule name and Prefix, then add each transition with its Storage class and days.
Press Create rule.

recipes.verify: The rule is listed under Lifecycle rules.

steps.say: Type S3 in the Search box at the top and open S3.
Choose General purpose buckets in the left navigation.
Open the bucket {1}.
Open the Management tab and read Lifecycle rules.

recipes.title: Create a VPC

steps.say: Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Your VPCs in the left navigation.
Press Create VPC.
Keep VPC only and type {1} in IPv4 CIDR.
Press Create VPC.

recipes.verify: The new VPC is listed with its VPC ID - copy it.

steps.say: Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Your VPCs in the left navigation.
Select the VPC {1}.
Open Actions and choose Delete VPC.
Confirm the deletion.
Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Your VPCs in the left navigation.
Read each VPC's IPv4 CIDR and Default VPC columns.

recipes.title: Create a subnet

steps.say: Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Subnets in the left navigation.
Press Create subnet.
Choose the VPC {1} in VPC ID.
Choose the Availability Zone {3}.
Type {2} in IPv4 subnet CIDR block.
Press Create subnet.

recipes.verify: The subnet is listed with its CIDR and Availability Zone.

steps.say: Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Subnets in the left navigation.
Read the Subnet ID, CIDR and Availability Zone of each row.
Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Route tables in the left navigation.
Select the route table {1}.
Press Edit routes.
Press Remove on the route to {2}.
Press Save changes.
Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Route tables in the left navigation.
Select the route table and read its Routes.

recipes.title: Create a VPC endpoint

steps.say: Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Endpoints in the left navigation.
Press Create endpoint.
Pick the service {2} under Services.
Choose the type {3}.
Choose the VPC {1} and tick its route tables or subnets.
Press Create endpoint.

recipes.verify: The endpoint is listed as Available.

steps.say: Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Endpoints in the left navigation.
Select the endpoint {1}.
Open Actions and choose Manage policy.
Choose Custom and paste the policy JSON from the file.
Press Save.
Type VPC in the Search box at the top and open VPC.
Choose Endpoints in the left navigation.
Read the endpoint IDs, types and status.

recipes.title: Create a security group

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Security Groups in the left navigation.
Press Create security group.
Type {1} as the Security group name.
Type the Description {3}.
Choose the VPC {2}.
Press Create security group.

recipes.verify: The group opens with its Security group ID - copy it.

recipes.title: Add an inbound rule

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Security Groups in the left navigation.
Open the security group {1}.
Press Edit inbound rules.
Press Add rule.
Choose Custom TCP (or the matching type) and type port {3}.
Choose Custom and type the source CIDR {4}.
Press Save rules.

recipes.verify: The rule is listed on the Inbound rules tab.

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Security Groups in the left navigation.
Open a group and read its Inbound rules tab.
Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Key Pairs in the left navigation.
Press Create key pair.
Type {1} as the Name.
Press Create key pair.
Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Key Pairs in the left navigation.
Read the key pair names and types.

recipes.title: Launch an instance

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Instances in the left navigation.
Press Launch instances.
Pick the AMI {1} under Application and OS Images.
Choose the Instance type {2}.
Choose the Key pair name {3}.
Set the Subnet and security group under Network settings if the task names them.
Press Launch instance.

recipes.verify: Success: the instance appears under Instances as Pending, then Running.

recipes.title: Start instance

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Instances in the left navigation.
Select the instance {1}.
Open Instance state and choose Start instance.

recipes.verify: The Instance state column shows Running.

recipes.title: Stop instance

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Instances in the left navigation.
Select the instance {1}.
Open Instance state and choose Stop instance.

recipes.verify: The Instance state column shows Stopped.

recipes.title: Terminate

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Instances in the left navigation.
Select the instance {1}.
Open Instance state and choose Terminate (delete) instance.
Press Terminate (delete) to confirm.

recipes.verify: The Instance state column shows Terminated.

recipes.title: Tag an instance

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Instances in the left navigation.
Select the instance {1}.
Open Actions > Instance settings > Manage tags.
Add the tag {2} with value {3}, and any other tags the task names.
Press Save.

recipes.verify: The Tags tab of the instance lists the new tags.

steps.say: Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose Instances in the left navigation.
Read the Instance ID and Instance state of each row.
Type EC2 in the Search box at the top and open EC2.
Choose AMIs in the left navigation.
Read the AMI IDs and names.

recipes.title: Create a role

steps.say: Type IAM in the Search box at the top and open IAM.
Choose Roles in the left navigation.
Press Create role.
Choose Custom trust policy and paste the trust policy from the file.
Press Next, add any permissions, and press Next again.
Type {1} as the Role name.
Press Create role.

recipes.verify: The role is listed under Roles.

recipes.title: Attach a policy to a role

steps.say: Type IAM in the Search box at the top and open IAM.
Choose Roles in the left navigation.
Open the role {1}.
Press Add permissions.
Search for {2} and tick it.
Press Add permissions to attach it.

recipes.verify: The policy is listed under Permissions policies.

steps.say: Type IAM in the Search box at the top and open IAM.
Choose Roles in the left navigation.
Open the role {1}.
Read the Permissions policies list.
Type IAM in the Search box at the top and open IAM.
Choose Roles in the left navigation.
Read the role names.

recipes.title: Create a function

steps.say: Type Lambda in the Search box at the top and open Lambda.
Choose Functions in the left navigation.
Press Create function.
Keep Author from scratch and type {1} as the Function name.
Choose the Runtime {2}.
Open Change default execution role, choose Use an existing role and pick the role.
Press Create function.

recipes.verify: The function page opens with a success banner.

steps.say: Type Lambda in the Search box at the top and open Lambda.
Choose Functions in the left navigation.
Open the function {1}.
Open the Test tab.
Press Test.
Read the response and the Log output.
Type Lambda in the Search box at the top and open Lambda.
Choose Functions in the left navigation.
Read the function names and runtimes.
Type CloudWatch in the Search box at the top and open CloudWatch.
Choose Log groups in the left navigation.
Open the log group {1}.
Read the log events.

recipes.title: Create a database

steps.say: Type RDS in the Search box at the top and open RDS.
Choose Databases in the left navigation.
Press Create database.
Choose the engine {2} under Engine options.
Type {1} as the DB instance identifier and set a master password.
Choose the DB instance class {3}.
Type {4} GiB in Allocated storage.
Press Create database.

recipes.verify: The database is listed under Databases.

steps.say: Type RDS in the Search box at the top and open RDS.
Choose Databases in the left navigation.
Open a database and read its endpoint and status.

recipes.title: Create a table

steps.say: Type DynamoDB in the Search box at the top and open DynamoDB.
Choose Tables in the left navigation.
Press Create table.
Type {1} as the Table name.
Type {2} as the Partition key and keep String.
Keep Default settings (on-demand) and press Create table.

recipes.verify: The table is listed and becomes Active.

steps.say: Type DynamoDB in the Search box at the top and open DynamoDB.
Choose Explore items in the left navigation.
Choose the table {1} on the left.
Press Create item.
Type each attribute value from the item JSON.
Press Create item.
Type DynamoDB in the Search box at the top and open DynamoDB.
Choose Tables in the left navigation.
Open the table {1}.
Read the Overview tab.
Type DynamoDB in the Search box at the top and open DynamoDB.
Choose Tables in the left navigation.
Read the table names.
Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Databases in the left navigation.
Press Add database.
Type {1} as the Name.
Type the Description {2}.
Press Create database.
Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Connections in the left navigation.
Press Create connection.
Fill in the name, Connection type, Subnet and Security group from the JSON file.
Press Create connection.
Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Crawlers in the left navigation.
Press Create crawler.
Type {1} as the Name.
Type {4} as the Data source - S3 path.
Choose the IAM role {2}.
Choose the Target database {3}.
Press Create crawler.

recipes.title: Run a crawler

steps.say: Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Crawlers in the left navigation.
Select the crawler {1}.
Press Run.

recipes.verify: The crawler shows Running, then Ready with the last run Succeeded.

steps.say: Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Crawlers in the left navigation.
Read the crawler {1} row: status and last run.
Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Jobs in the left navigation.
Open the job {1}.
Press Reset job bookmark.

recipes.title: Run a Glue job

steps.say: Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Jobs in the left navigation.
Open the job {1}.
Press Run.
Read the new row on the Runs tab.

recipes.verify: A new run appears on the Runs tab and ends Succeeded.

steps.say: Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Jobs in the left navigation.
Open the job {1}.
Open the Job details tab.
Change the fields the update file names (for example Job parameters).
Press Save.
Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Jobs in the left navigation.
Open the job {1}.
Read the newest row on the Runs tab: its state and error.
Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Tables in the left navigation.
Open the table {2} of database {1}.
Open the Partitions tab.
Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Tables in the left navigation.
Open the table {2} of database {1}.
Read the Schema and Table properties tabs.

recipes.title: See the tables of a database

steps.say: Type AWS Glue in the Search box at the top and open AWS Glue.
Choose Tables in the left navigation.
Read the tables whose Database is {1}.
Type Athena in the Search box at the top and open Athena.
Choose Workgroups in the left navigation.
Press Create workgroup.
Type {1} as the Workgroup name.
Type {2} as the Location of query result.
Tick Override client-side settings and Publish query metrics to AWS CloudWatch.
Press Create workgroup.
Type Athena in the Search box at the top and open Athena.
Choose Workgroups in the left navigation.
Select the workgroup {1}.
Press Edit.
Set Per query data usage control to 1 GB and keep Override client-side settings on.
Press Save changes.
Type Athena in the Search box at the top and open Athena.
Choose Workgroups in the left navigation.
Read the settings of the workgroup {1}.
Type Athena in the Search box at the top and open Athena.
Choose Query editor in the left navigation.
Choose the workgroup {1}.
Type the query in the editor.
Press Run.
Read Query results: status and data scanned.
Type Athena in the Search box at the top and open Athena.
Choose Query editor in the left navigation.
Open the Recent queries tab.
Read the status, data scanned and error of the query.
Type Lake Formation in the Search box at the top and open Lake Formation.
Choose Data lake locations in the left navigation.
Press Register location.
Type s3://{1} as the Amazon S3 path.
Keep the service-linked role and press Register location.
Type Lake Formation in the Search box at the top and open Lake Formation.
Choose Data lake permissions in the left navigation.
Find the IAMAllowedPrincipals row for the table.
Press Revoke.
Type Lake Formation in the Search box at the top and open Lake Formation.
Choose Data lake permissions in the left navigation.
Filter by the principal and read its permissions.

recipes.title: Create a KMS key

steps.say: Type Key Management Service in the Search box at the top and open Key Management Service.
Choose Customer managed keys in the left navigation.
Press Create key.
Keep Symmetric and Encrypt and decrypt.
Type the Description {1} and add the tag.
Press Finish.

recipes.verify: The key is listed - copy its Key ID.

recipes.title: Add an alias to a key

steps.say: Type Key Management Service in the Search box at the top and open Key Management Service.
Choose Customer managed keys in the left navigation.
Open the key.
Open the Aliases tab.
Type {1} as the new alias.
Press Create alias.
Type Key Management Service in the Search box at the top and open Key Management Service.
Choose Customer managed keys in the left navigation.
Open the key {1}.
Open the Key rotation tab.
Turn on the Automatic key rotation switch (or read whether it is Enabled).
Type Key Management Service in the Search box at the top and open Key Management Service.
Choose Customer managed keys in the left navigation.
Open the key {1}.
On the Key policy tab press Edit.
Paste the policy JSON from the file.
Press Save changes.
Type Key Management Service in the Search box at the top and open Key Management Service.
Choose Customer managed keys in the left navigation.
Open the key {1}.
Read the Key policy tab.
Type Kinesis in the Search box at the top and open Kinesis.
Choose Data streams in the left navigation.
Press Create data stream.
Type {1} as the Data stream name.
Choose Provisioned and set {2} shards.
Press Create data stream.
Type Kinesis in the Search box at the top and open Kinesis.
Choose Data streams in the left navigation.
Open the stream {1}.
Open the Put record tab.
Type a Partition key and the Data of one record from the file.
Press Put record (repeat for each record).
Type Kinesis in the Search box at the top and open Kinesis.
Choose Data streams in the left navigation.
Open the stream.
Open the Data viewer tab and choose the Shard and Trim horizon.
Press Get records.
Type Kinesis in the Search box at the top and open Kinesis.
Choose Data streams in the left navigation.
Open the stream {1}.
Read the Data stream summary and the Shards tab.
Type CloudWatch in the Search box at the top and open CloudWatch.
Choose All alarms in the left navigation.
Select the alarm {1}.
Open Actions and choose Set state: In alarm (test actions).

recipes.title: See an alarm and its history

steps.say: Type CloudWatch in the Search box at the top and open CloudWatch.
Choose All alarms in the left navigation.
Open the alarm {1}.
Read its state and the History list.
Type SNS in the Search box at the top and open SNS.
Choose Topics in the left navigation.
Open the topic.
Read the Subscriptions table.
Type Amazon Redshift in the Search box at the top and open Amazon Redshift.
Choose Serverless dashboard in the left navigation.
Press Create workgroup.
Type {1} as the Workgroup name.
Set Base capacity (RPUs) to {3}.
Type {2} as the Namespace name.
Press Create.
Type Amazon Redshift in the Search box at the top and open Amazon Redshift.
Choose Serverless dashboard in the left navigation.
Read the workgroup {1} in the Workgroups table.
Type Amazon Redshift in the Search box at the top and open Amazon Redshift.
Choose Query editor v2 in the left navigation.
Type the SQL statement in the editor.
Press Run.
Read the Result: Finished means it worked.
Type Amazon Redshift in the Search box at the top and open Amazon Redshift.
Choose Query editor v2 in the left navigation.
Read the status in the Result panel.
Type Step Functions in the Search box at the top and open Step Functions.
Choose State machines in the left navigation.
Press Create state machine.
Type {1} as the State machine name.
Choose the Execution role {2}.
Paste the Definition from the file.
Press Create.
Type Step Functions in the Search box at the top and open Step Functions.
Choose State machines in the left navigation.
Open the state machine.
Open the execution in the Executions table and read its Status.
Type Billing and Cost Management in the Search box at the top and open Billing and Cost Management.
Choose Cost allocation tags in the left navigation.
Find the tag key {1}.
Press Activate on its row.
Type Billing and Cost Management in the Search box at the top and open Billing and Cost Management.
Choose Cost allocation tags in the left navigation.
Set Backfill from to {1}.
Press Backfill tags.
Type Billing and Cost Management in the Search box at the top and open Billing and Cost Management.
Choose Cost Explorer in the left navigation.
Set Start to {1} and End to {2}.
Keep Granularity Monthly and choose Group by {4} ({3}).
Press Apply and read the breakdown.
Type Billing and Cost Management in the Search box at the top and open Billing and Cost Management.
Choose Budgets in the left navigation.
Read the budgets and their amounts.

recipes.title: See who you are signed in as

steps.say: Open the account menu at the right of the top bar.
Read Account ID and IAM user.
